name: Dive cleanly into a pool
blurb: A clean, quiet dive with no belly-flop is a shape problem: hands lead, head is tucked between the arms, and the body follows in one line.
gear: A pool with adequate depth — check it before every dive
steps: Check depth first, every single time and at every new pool. Shallow-water diving causes catastrophic spinal injuries.
Start kneeling on the edge: arms extended overhead, hands stacked, head tucked between them, and topple in fingers first.
Progress to a crouch, then one knee, then standing.
Aim at a spot in the water about a metre and a half out, not straight down.
Keep your body in one straight line and point your toes — the splash tells you how well you did.
Practise the entry angle: too flat and you slap, too steep and you go straight to the bottom.
tips: Never dive into water of unknown depth, ever — not lakes, not the shallow end, not the sea.
Lifting your head at the last second is what causes belly-flops. Keep it tucked.
proof: A quiet, straight dive from standing that leaves almost no splash.
